findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: The `isTeamAdminOrOwner` flag is built with a logical AND of `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, but the variable name and intent (`AdminOrOwner`) clearly indicates OR. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner fails the check (the only users who pass are owners, since being an owner typically implies being an admin). Any non-owner team admin (e.g. a delegated team manager) is silently denied permission even though the UI label and code path assume they can add guests.

findings.title: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive while blacklist is lowercased
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased via `.toLowerCase()` on line 71, but the subsequent filter compares raw user input: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. A guest like `Bad@Example.com` is not matched against a blacklist entry `bad@example.com`, so any address whose case differs from the configured blacklist bypasses it entirely. Normalize the guest email (and ideally emails throughout the handler) to lowercase before comparing.

findings.title: No transaction / no error handling around calendar sync after DB update
findings.body: `prisma.booking.update` writes the new attendees to the database first. `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is then awaited with no try/catch. If the calendar integration throws (rate limit, expired token, network, etc.), the function rejects with a 500, but the database already has the new attendees persisted. Result: the Cal.com booking now lists guests that are NOT on the linked Google/Outlook calendar, and the user has no way to roll back. The whole flow should be wrapped in a transaction or, at minimum, the calendar sync should happen first so a failure leaves the system consistent.

findings.title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests without organizer consent
findings.body: Permission grants the addGuests capability not only to organizers and team admins/owners but also to any attendee (`isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(a => a.email === user.email)`). Combined with the lack of rate limiting, any invitee can enumerate or spam-add external email addresses to someone else's meeting. There is no confirmation from the organizer, and the organizer is only informed after the fact via `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail`. Either remove the attendee branch or require organizer approval.

findings.title: No check on booking status before mutating
findings.body: The handler never inspects `booking.status` or `booking.endTime`. It will happily persist new attendees onto CANCELLED, REJECTED, or already-finished bookings, and `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` will then either fail or silently modify a calendar event for a meeting that no longer exists. The handler should reject mutations on non-ACCEPTED or past bookings.

findings.title: Email send uses raw input guests instead of filtered uniqueGuests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the original input list rather than `uniqueGuests` (which excludes already-attending emails and blacklisted addresses). In `email-manager.ts` the recipient loop checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide between sending a fresh `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs. an `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. As a result, an existing attendee whose email is also present in the input gets a full "you're scheduled" confirmation email (with ICS file) instead of a "guests added" notification, and any email in the input that wasn't actually added is still considered "new" for routing. Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other send* function in this file honors `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (read from the event type metadata). `sendAddGuestsEmails` accepts no metadata and never checks these flags, so it always sends the organizer and attendee notifications regardless of how the event type is configured. Either thread the metadata through from the handler or look it up via the booking's eventType.

findings.title: attendees[0].name accessed without null check in email subject
findings.body: The subject template reads `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. If `attendees` is empty this throws a TypeError that aborts the email; if `attendees[0].name` is null/undefined the subject renders as "Guests Added: <eventType> with  at <date>". Add a guard or fall back to the organizer/team name.

findings.title: isInvalidEmail flag is not cleared after a successful mutation
findings.body: On validation failure `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is called, but neither `onSuccess` nor `handleAdd` ever resets it back to false. A user who first submits invalid emails, then fixes them and successfully adds guests, will continue to see the red "Emails must be unique and valid" banner in the dialog (and after reopening the dialog for the same booking) until the Cancel button is clicked. Reset the flag at the start of `handleAdd` and inside `onSuccess`.

findings.title: Initial state seeds an empty string, so the first Add always fails validation
findings.body: `useState<string[]>([""])` initializes the input with one empty email. The zod schema `z.array(z.string().email())` rejects empty strings, so clicking "Add" with the default state always shows the error banner before the user has even had a chance to type. Initialize with an empty array (matching `MultiEmail`'s empty-state branch) and add the empty input only after the user clicks "Add Emails".

findings.title: addGuests uses authedProcedure instead of bookingsProcedure
findings.body: Sibling mutations that touch a booking (`editLocation`, `confirm`, etc.) use `bookingsProcedure`, which typically enforces booking-level permission middleware. `addGuests` is wired with the looser `authedProcedure`, so any authenticated user can hit the endpoint and the only authorization is the handler's own checks (which have the bugs noted above). Use `bookingsProcedure` for consistency and to inherit the centralized guards.

findings.title: Email-send errors are swallowed with console.log
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discards the error object entirely (notice `console.log` rather than `console.error`, and `err` is not used). Use `logger.error(...)` from `@calcom/lib/logger` like the rest of the file, and include `err` so the failure is diagnosable in production.

findings.title: Direct reassignment of a prop
findings.body: `value = value || [];` mutates the `value` prop in place. While React does not re-render on prop mutation, this is misleading code and means subsequent reads use the mutated object reference. Use a default parameter (`value = []` in the signature) or a local `const emails = value ?? []`.

findings.title: Using array index as React key in the email list
findings.body: `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index} ...)` reuses keys when emails are added/removed, which causes React to reuse input components and can lose focus/caret position or render stale values for the newly inserted empty input. Use a stable id (e.g. include the email value or a counter ref).
